% The top-level itemize label is `\textbullet`. pdf-inspector 0.2.6 keeps the
% bullet as U+2022 ("•") only when it merges into the following text run;
% with the default \labelsep the bullet is emitted as its own leading run on
% some TeX Live versions (2023/Debian), which pdf-inspector then normalizes to
% "-" and the U+2022 assertion fails. Zeroing \labelsep forces the bullet to
% merge with the item text, so the extracted marker is "•" consistently on CI
% (TeX Live 2023) and macOS (TeX Live 2026).
\setlength{\labelsep}{0pt}

\section{Shopping and Tasks}
This list-heavy fixture exercises both \texttt{itemize} and \texttt{enumerate}
environments, including nested lists, so that the tests can confirm bulleted
and numbered content is extracted as readable text.

\subsection{Bullet Points}
\begin{itemize}
  \item The first bullet item mentions the unique marker
        \texttt{listsentinel-quark}.
  \item A second ordinary bullet about stacking the shelves and tidying the
        pantry before the weekend.
  \item A third bullet that wraps across multiple lines to ensure that
        line-wrapped list text is extracted as a single logical item rather
        than being split awkwardly.
  \begin{itemize}
    \item A nested bullet under the third item, carrying the marker
          \texttt{listsentinel-nested}.
    \item Another nested bullet without a marker, purely for depth.
  \end{itemize}
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Numbered Steps}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item The first enumerated step references the marker
        \texttt{listsentinel-neutrino}.
  \item The second step requires mixing the reagents and stirring gently for
        at least ten minutes.
  \item The third step repeats the marker \texttt{listsentinel-neutrino} to
        reinforce the assertion that enumerated content is preserved.
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item A nested numbered sub-step beneath the third item.
  \end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
